subject: Tyonek affiliate past performance counts only when the documentation is attached
body:
Tyonek runs 22 federal registrations under one parent so one attachment decides whose record counts. RFP FA8773-25-R-0002 says an affiliate's record "shall not be evaluated or considered" without it.

We've already done the study on how to measure that exposure.

https://alaskaaihq.com/awesomeproposal/tyonek-native-corporation/

Tell us if it's useful or pass it along.
title_note: Director of Marketing and Communications, published on tyonek.com/contact and corroborated in the press-contact block of the 10 October 2024 Coast Guard release. She is a ROUTER, not the buyer, and she sits at the Alabama operating campus rather than Anchorage, so the email is written to be forwarded, names nobody, and assumes neither that she owns capture nor that she is in Alaska.
opens_on: Tyonek holds 22 separate federal registrations under one parent with near duplicate names across states, against RFP FA8773-25-R-0002's provision that an affiliate's past performance 'shall not be evaluated or considered' without the documentation proving the affiliation in the proposal.
lead_critic: ship on round 4. Round 1 was killed for opening on a document rather than on them, for claiming records could drop out 'with no notice' when GAO dismissed the protest precisely because the provision was unambiguously clear, and for an ask that gave up the reply. Round 2 fixed all of that and introduced a new defect, a sentence about the build we priced, which is the compressed twin of a line Talon cut by hand on a real send, plus an ask for half a day smuggled in ahead of the value. Round 3 cut that sentence and moved the defect rather than killing it, promising the study answers what the attachment costs when the study's actual finding is that the exposure is unmeasured. Round 4 promises only what the study delivers.
